Own newsletter calls the employer credit expansion (HEA 1177) too small and backs a blocked proposal to require release of CCDF voucher funds; shows a lean toward more public subsidy but names no reach (income levels, universality, provider grants) that separates rungs 1-3; his own vote on HEA 1177 or the SEA 4 amendment is not shown.
Criticizes delay and cuts to child care funding and voucher wait lists; a pro-funding lean with no rung clause.
Objects to CCDF reimbursement-rate cuts for low-income voucher families and calls for revamping the child care system; direction toward more support, no rung separated.

rows.reasoning: His own newsletters oppose CCDF voucher reimbursement cuts and back a proposal that "would have required the release of funds to alleviate the child care crisis", placing him on the more-public-support side. None of his words says whether support should reach every family regardless of income, low- and middle-income families with provider grants, or only families below a set threshold, so rungs 1-3 are not separated.
